reason: The goal is to eat from the garden, and cutting lettuce is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect to harvest lettuce leaves that can be prepared at the galley.

effect: The scissors produced lettuce leaves, so they are ready to take to the galley.
reason: Preparing the harvested leaves at the galley should satisfy the goal of eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the lettuce, though I don't know what the meal will be.

alternatives.reason: I considered harvesting more, but already have leaves to prepare.

effect: The lettuce became supper, completing the chapter’s goal and showing that the garden survived well enough to provide food.
reaction: The crunch in the message to Mara was a satisfying small detail after the long storm.

mostWorthwhile.text: Preparing the supper was most worthwhile: it gave a tangible payoff to keeping the garden alive and a small connection with Mara.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was straightforward, and its result added little beyond confirming the harvest.

surprise.text: The voice message sent with the first crunch was an unexpected personal detail.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; harvesting leaves and taking them to the galley both had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I want to learn how the storm and the return journey unfold, although this chapter offered little in the way of gameplay decisions.
